title: Houthis release the 25 crew of the Galaxy Leader after more than a year in detention
body:
On 22 January 2025 the United Nations Special Envoy for Yemen, Hans Grundberg, and the International Maritime Organization welcomed the release of the 25 crew members of the car carrier MV Galaxy Leader, which the Houthis had seized in the Red Sea in November 2023. The sailors had been held for more than a year. Grundberg called the release "heartwarming news" that ended the arbitrary detention and separation of the crew and their families, and described it as "a step in the right direction."

The Galaxy Leader was seized on 19 November 2023, when the Houthis took the Bahamas-flagged vehicle carrier about 150 kilometres off the port of Hodeidah, according to The Times of Israel. The crew came from Ukraine, Bulgaria, the Philippines and Mexico, and Israeli officials said no Israelis were aboard. The ship was registered to a British company partly owned by Israeli businessman Abraham "Rami" Ungar and was leased to a Japanese company at the time. The seizure opened the Houthi campaign against Red Sea shipping.

Grundberg urged the Houthis to continue by ending all maritime attacks, and thanked Oman for its persistent efforts to advocate for the crew's release. He noted that the Houthis were still holding more than 60 staff of UN agencies, international organisations and diplomatic missions, all Yemeni nationals, for more than a year. IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez called the release a moment of relief and credited collective diplomacy and dialogue. The ship itself was struck on 17 March 2025 during the US air campaign, according to the Houthi-aligned Saba news agency.
